title: Kindness for Gran
lines: Gran was coming to stay with Meg for a week.
Her room was up the steps at the back.
Meg ran up to look at it first.
The room was dark and it felt cold.
"I want to fix it up for Gran," she told Dad.
Meg picked red flowers from the yard.
She set them on the shelf by the bed.
But by lunch the flowers had gone limp.
Meg felt a big sadness about that.
Then Dad handed her a small lamp.
Meg set it on the shelf and lit it.
The darkness went away and the room felt warm.
She got a thick quilt and made the bed.
Dad helped her sweep the floor as well.
Gran came at six with a big red bag.
She went up the steps and looked in.
"What kindness!" said Gran. "This room is bright."
Meg's sadness had turned into happiness.
Gran sat on the bed and held her hand.
Now Meg fills that room with flowers each week.

questions.ask: What did Meg try first to fix up the room?
questions.listenFor: She picked red flowers and set them on the shelf. By lunch they had gone limp.

questions.ask: What did Dad hand Meg, and what did it do?
questions.listenFor: A small lamp. It took the darkness away and made the room feel warm. Sadness, happiness, kindness - -ness turns a describing word into a thing.

questions.ask: What would you do for someone at home who felt sad? Why?
questions.listenFor: Any kind answer counts. You are listening for the because part, not for a right idea.
